x: Alan Sexton won the 220 yds. and Basil Walden won the 440, while Bob Belmore and Steve Charlton were 2nd and 3rd in the 1 mile match. We also won the 4 x 110 yds. relay and the final match points were—Belgrave H., 45; Essex Beagles, 25; Hercules A.C., 19.

Walker on once again being selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties c.c. race, also to Bob Belmore, who is a second-claim member, and to Jack Brown, who was a scoring member of the Kent team, who were third in the team championship.
Jack Brown won the 1½ miles in another new track record time of 6 mins. 58.2 secs., while in the 3 mile event we had Bob Belmore 4th and Don Maclean 5th.

In second place was our second-claim member, Bob Belmore, who did 31 mins. 33.4 secs. The County Pentathlon Championship was another event to be decided and in this Alan Law was the winner with a total of 1,302 pts
Walker ran well to win the 1 mile in the good time of 4 mins. 22 secs. Bob Belmore turned out for us in the 2 mile run and was 3rd, with Maynard, of H.H.H., doing 9 mins. 23.5 secs.
Walker, who had made the pace in the early stages of the race, was second, with Bill Lucas, still retired, in third place. Then came Ray Tooby, John Bromley, Bob Belmore, Ron Linstead, G.

Highlight of the afternoon was a magnificent run by Pat Newell who got the bronze medal in the over 60's only just behind Bob Belmore. Pat beat a rather off-form Charlie Walker by over a minute, the first time that he had beaten his friend since rejoining Belgrave last Spring.
